subject: Optimize toolkit — license alignment, quantization validation & crediting flow
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@atlashealth.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit questions for Atlas procurement

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team found the batching/caching examples helpful. A few procurement questions came up after the session: 1) we need a clear way to map credits to our expected monthly token usage (we run two daily ETL jobs and a live inference lane), 2) can you confirm whether quantized model variants are allowed under the same license, and 3) what levers exist to keep tail latency under 250ms for our near-realtime flows?

Also attaching the procurement template — happy to run through the fields with you live.

Samira
Head of ML Ops, Atlas Health
(attachment: atlas_procurement_template.xlsx)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit questions for Atlas procurement

Samira — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: credits map to billed token-equivalents (we'll share a worked example), yes you can serve quantized variants under the same customer license (we treat them as model variants), and we have a latency playbook (prefix caching + micro-batching + GPU pinning) that typically keeps P95 under 200ms for workloads like yours.

I'll put together a small MOC that maps your ETL + live lanes to recommended packaging and a suggested credits bucket. Marissa, Karthik — can you validate the quantization guidance (we recommended int8 + KV-cache friendly layout) and confirm if that requires a change to the SLA addendum?

Grace
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | https://redwood.com
(attachment: atlas_optimize_moc_v1.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit questions for Atlas procurement

On the quantization question — confirmed: serving a quantized variant (we recommend asymmetric int8 + per-channel scales for your model family) is covered by the same commercial license. Operational caveats: 1) cold-start generation quality should be validated with a small prompt-set (attached prompt examples), 2) if Atlas requires cross-region fallbacks to FP16 variants we should add a small egress/variant usage line in the SLA. I flagged a short SLA addendum (sla_addendum.docx) that outlines variant fallbacks and latency SLOs for multi-variant routing.

Karthik — any objection to calling out a 5% quality buffer allowance during rollout?

Marissa
Director, Product Strategy, Redwood Optimize
(attachment: atlas_prompt_set_example.jsonl)

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@atlashealth.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit questions for Atlas procurement

Thanks Grace/Marissa. Procurement is fine with quantized variants under the same license, but they want: 1) a worked example that shows how credits are consumed for (a) a 2M token monthly ETL job (batched) and (b) a 250k token/month live lane (low-latency), 2) explicit language for fallbacks to FP16 that doesn't trigger overage fees during regional outages, and 3) a clear audit trail we can push to our security team about KV caching and retention.

Can we please get the worked credit mapping and an updated SLA addendum by EOD Monday? Also — is there any flexibility on upfront credits / committed discount? Procurement is motivated by a predictable monthly bill.

Samira

On Fri, May 21, 2027 at 09:05 AM Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Samira — looping in Dylan and Karthik to get the worked examples and finalize the SLA language. I'm also adding Marissa for the quality buffer callout.
>
> Grace

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit questions for Atlas procurement

Samira — attaching the worked credit examples and an annotated cost table. Two quick notes: 1) For the batched ETL lane I recommend a daily batching window with KV prefix caching — in our model that reduces billed tokens by approximately 32% versus naive runs. The attached MOC includes a conservative 20% uplift to account for prompt variance. 2) For the live lane, set the batch timeout very small (5–10ms) and enable micro-batching on the VPC path; that preserves P95 latency while still allowing some batching efficiency.

I also sketched two commercial options: a) 12-month commitment with a 15% committed discount + 10% onboarding credit; b) month-to-month with slightly higher per-token rate but no commitment. Procurement preference tends to go with option (a) for predictability.

Attachments: atlas_optimize_credits_worked_examples.xlsx, sla_addendum.docx

--
Dylan Brooks
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

On Sat, May 22, 2027 at 15:05 Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com> wrote:

Grace/Dylan — this looks good overall. Procurement asked me to confirm one final operational question before they sign: during multi-variant fallbacks (quantized -> FP16), how will usage be attributed to credits versus overage triggers? If you can confirm the attribution model and sign off on the SLA language we can route the commercial terms to legal next week.

I appreciate the responsiveness — Atlas would like an answer (and a final redline) by Monday close of business.

Samira
